title: Forms IX (ifʿalla) & X (istafʿala)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 23; Ryding Ch. 30–31)
objectives: Recognize Form IX (اِفْعَلَّ) for colors and fixed physical characteristics.
Conjugate Form X (اِسْتَفْعَلَ) and identify its seeking/requesting/considering semantics.
Form Form X maṣādir (اِسْتِفْعَالٌ) and active/passive participles (مُسْتَفْعِلٌ / مُسْتَفْعَلٌ).
recallPrompt: From Chapter 22: What underlying root hides behind a Form VIII verb beginning with اِتَّـ?

sections.heading: Colors/Traits (Form IX) & Seeking/Requesting (Form X)
sections.body: Form IX (اِفْعَلَّ) doubles the final radical and is restricted to colors and bodily traits (e.g., اِحْمَرَّ 'to turn red'). Form X (اِسْتَفْعَلَ) prefixes اِسْتَـ and is one of the most productive stems in Classical Arabic, expressing seeking, asking for, or deeming something to possess a quality.

sections.label: Form X Semantics & Morphology
sections.summary: Form X adds اِسْتَـ to the root (e.g., غ-ف-ر 'forgive' → اِسْتَغْفَرَ 'seek forgiveness'). Like doubled verbs, Form IX separates its doubled C3 before consonant suffixes (اِحْمَرَرْتُ).

sections.translation: The believer sought forgiveness from his Lord.
sections.irab: اِسْتَغْفَرَ: فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ (وَزْنُ اِسْتَفْعَلَ، جَذْرُ غ-ف-ر) | المُؤْمِنُ: فَاعِلٌ مَرْفُوعٌ | رَبَّهُ: مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ مَنْصُوبٌ
sections.notes: Strip اِسْتَـ from اِسْتَغْفَرَ to recover the root غ-ف-ر.

sections.heading: Active Participle of Form X
sections.body: Replacing يَـ with مُـ and placing kasrah before the final radical yields مُسْتَغْفِرٌ ('one seeking forgiveness').
